tracks.name: Mobile
tracks.short_description: Build apps people carry in their pocket.
tracks.profile: Mobile developers build apps for phones and tablets. They enjoy making something friends and family can install and use every day, care about how an app feels to touch, and like testing ideas on a real device right away.

videos.title: A day as a mobile developer

tracks.name: Frontend
tracks.short_description: Build the screens people see and click.
tracks.profile: Frontend developers build the part of websites and apps that people see and click. They enjoy seeing their work on screen right away, like both how things look and how they work, and turn designs into real pages with code.

videos.title: From design to a real web page

tracks.name: Backend
tracks.short_description: Build the engine behind apps: data, logic and servers.
tracks.profile: Backend developers build the hidden engine of apps: servers, databases and the rules that decide what happens when a user presses a button. They enjoy solving logic puzzles, organising information and making things work reliably.

videos.title: What happens after you press Send

tracks.name: UI/UX
tracks.short_description: Design apps that are clear, beautiful and easy to use.
tracks.profile: UI/UX designers decide how an app looks and how easy it is to use. They enjoy drawing, choosing colours and layouts, watching how people use things and making confusing things simple.

tracks.name: AI
tracks.short_description: Teach computers to learn from examples.
tracks.profile: AI engineers build programs that learn from examples, such as recognising pictures or understanding speech. They enjoy maths, patterns, asking why things happen and experimenting until a model gets better.

videos.title: How a computer learns from examples

tracks.name: Testing
tracks.profile: Software testers find problems before users do. They enjoy noticing small details, trying unusual things to see what breaks, explaining problems clearly and making sure a product is safe to release.

videos.title: The detective work of software testing

tracks.name: Data
tracks.short_description: Turn numbers into answers and charts.
tracks.profile: Data analysts turn numbers into answers. They enjoy finding patterns, making charts, asking questions like which is the most popular and using facts to help people decide.

tracks.name: Gaming
tracks.short_description: Create the games you want to play.
tracks.profile: Game developers create games: the rules, the characters, the levels and the code that makes them move. They enjoy playing and imagining games, telling stories, and tuning things until they are fun.

lessons.title: Elements and tags
lessons.concept:
A page is built from elements like

,

and , each opened and closed with tags.

lessons.title: Links, images and lists
lessons.concept: Attributes like href, src and alt give elements their address and meaning.

lessons.title: Forms and semantic HTML
lessons.concept: Forms collect input, and semantic tags like <header>, <nav> and <main> explain the page's parts.

lessons.title: Selectors and colours
lessons.concept: CSS rules pick elements with selectors and set properties like color and font-size.

lessons.title: The box model
lessons.concept: Every element is a box of content, padding, border and margin.

lessons.title: Flexbox and responsive design
lessons.concept: Flexbox lines up items in a row or column, and media queries change styles for small screens.

lessons.title: Variables
lessons.concept: variables
lessons.try_it_starter_code:
let x = 4;
console.log(3 * x + 2);

school_link.subject: Math
school_link.title: Substituting values in expressions
school_link.bridge_text: In code, a variable is the same as x in algebra: a name that holds a value you can use in a calculation.

lessons.title: Functions
lessons.concept: functions

school_link.subject: Math
school_link.title: Linear functions
school_link.bridge_text: A function in code works like f(x) in maths: you give it an input and it returns an output.

lessons.title: Conditions
lessons.concept: conditions

school_link.subject: Math
school_link.title: Inequalities
school_link.school_example: Is 2x + 3 > 10 when x = 4? 2 × 4 + 3 = 11, and 11 > 10, so yes
school_link.bridge_text: An if in code checks an inequality, just like at school, and then chooses what to do.

lessons.title: Functions with two inputs
lessons.concept: functions

school_link.subject: Science
school_link.title: Speed, distance and time
school_link.school_example: speed = distance ÷ time, so 120 km in 2 h = 60 km/h
school_link.bridge_text: A function can take two inputs, like distance and time, and return one answer: the speed.

lessons.title: Classes and components
lessons.concept: Bootstrap gives ready classes like btn and card, so you style by adding class names.

lessons.title: The grid system
lessons.concept: Rows hold 12 columns; col-md-6 takes half the row on medium screens and up.

lessons.title: Utilities and customising
lessons.concept: Utility classes like mt-3 and d-flex style quickly, and Sass variables change Bootstrap's theme.

lessons.title: Utility classes
lessons.concept: Each Tailwind class does one thing, like p-4 for padding or text-lg for font size.

lessons.title: Responsive and states
lessons.concept: Prefixes like md: and hover: apply a class only on bigger screens or on hover.

lessons.title: Theme and components
lessons.concept: The Tailwind config adds your own colours, and you reuse class sets as components.

lessons.title: Components and JSX
lessons.concept: A component is a function that returns JSX, which looks like HTML inside JavaScript.

lessons.title: Props and state
lessons.concept: Props pass data into a component; state is data a component remembers and changes.

lessons.title: Effects and fetching data
lessons.concept: useEffect runs code after rendering, for example to load data from an API.

lessons.title: Components and templates
lessons.concept: An Angular component has a TypeScript class and an HTML template that shows its data.

lessons.title: Binding and directives
lessons.concept: Bindings connect the class and the template; directives like *ngFor repeat elements.

lessons.title: Services and routing
lessons.concept: Services hold shared logic like API calls, and the router shows a component for each URL.

lessons.title: Pages and routing
lessons.concept: In the Next.js app folder, each folder with a page file becomes a URL.

lessons.title: Server and client components
lessons.concept: Server components render on the server; add "use client" for state and clicks in the browser.

lessons.title: Data, images and deployment
lessons.concept: Next.js caches data, optimises images with next/image and deploys easily, for example on Vercel.

lessons.title: Variables and types
lessons.concept: C# variables have a type, like int for whole numbers and string for text.

lessons.title: Methods and classes
lessons.concept: A class groups data and methods; an object is one thing made from a class.

lessons.title: Lists, LINQ and async
lessons.concept: LINQ filters and sorts lists, and async/await waits for slow work like a database without blocking.

lessons.title: Tables and SELECT
lessons.concept: A database keeps data in tables of rows and columns, and SELECT reads it.

lessons.title: Keys and JOIN
lessons.concept: A primary key identifies each row, and a JOIN combines rows from two tables by their keys.

lessons.title: Indexes and transactions
lessons.concept: Indexes make searches fast, and transactions make several changes happen all together or not at all.

lessons.title: HTTP and JSON
lessons.concept: Apps send HTTP requests like GET and POST, and APIs answer with JSON and a status code.

lessons.title: Endpoints and controllers
lessons.concept: In ASP.NET Core a controller method answers one route, like GET /api/v1/tracks.

lessons.title: Validation and errors
lessons.concept: Good APIs check input and answer with clear errors, like 400 with the field that is wrong.

lessons.title: Passwords and hashing
lessons.concept: Servers store a hash of each password, never the password itself.

lessons.title: Tokens and sessions
lessons.concept: After sign-in the server gives a token (like a JWT) that the app sends with each request.

lessons.title: Common attacks
lessons.concept: Know attacks like SQL injection and XSS, and stop them with parameters, encoding and checks.

lessons.title: Automated tests
lessons.concept: Tests run your code with known inputs and check the result, every time you change something.

lessons.title: Configuration and environments
lessons.concept: The same app runs in Development and Production with different settings, kept out of the code.

lessons.title: CI/CD and monitoring
lessons.concept: A pipeline builds, tests and deploys automatically, and health checks and logs show if the app is well.

lessons.title: Screens and touch
lessons.concept: Mobile screens are small and touched with fingers, so buttons are big and layouts simple.

lessons.title: Navigation patterns
lessons.concept: Apps move between screens with stacks, tabs and drawers, and the back gesture returns.

lessons.title: Accessibility and dark mode
lessons.concept: Good apps support screen readers, larger text and dark mode.

lessons.title: Widgets
lessons.concept: In Flutter everything on screen is a widget, like Text, Row and Button.

lessons.title: Stateful widgets
lessons.concept: A StatefulWidget keeps data that changes; setState redraws it.

lessons.title: Navigation and APIs
lessons.concept: Navigator moves between screens, and the http package loads data from APIs with async code.

lessons.title: Core components
lessons.concept: React Native uses View, Text and Pressable instead of div, p and button.
lessons.try_it_starter_code:
const screens = ['Home', 'Search', 'Profile'];
console.log(screens.indexOf('Profile') + 1);

lessons.title: Lists and state
lessons.concept: FlatList shows long lists fast, and useState keeps what the user types or chooses.

lessons.title: Device features
lessons.concept: Apps ask permission to use the camera or location, and save data on the phone for offline use.

lessons.title: Testing on devices
lessons.concept: Test on real phones of different sizes, not only on the simulator.

lessons.title: App stores
lessons.concept: Google Play and the App Store review apps and need icons, screenshots and a privacy policy.

lessons.title: Updates and feedback
lessons.concept: After launch, crash reports, ratings and analytics show what to fix next.

lessons.title: Visual hierarchy
lessons.concept: Size, colour and position show what matters most on a screen.

lessons.title: Colour and typography
lessons.concept: Pick a small palette and readable fonts, and keep enough contrast.

lessons.title: Consistency and design systems
lessons.concept: Reusable components and rules keep every screen consistent.

lessons.title: Knowing your users
lessons.concept: Talk to real users to learn their goals and problems before designing.

lessons.title: User journeys
lessons.concept: A journey map shows each step a user takes and how they feel along the way.

lessons.title: Usability testing
lessons.concept: Watch users try tasks with your design and note where they hesitate.

lessons.title: Sketching layouts
lessons.concept: Quick sketches let you try many layouts before choosing one.

lessons.title: User flows
lessons.concept: A flow connects screens in the order a user moves through a task.

lessons.title: Information architecture
lessons.concept: Organise and name content so users find what they need.

lessons.title: Frames and shapes
lessons.concept: Frames are screens; you draw shapes and text inside them.

lessons.title: Auto layout
lessons.concept: Auto layout makes frames grow and space items automatically, like flexbox.

lessons.title: Components and variants
lessons.concept: Components are reusable; variants hold states like default, hover and disabled.

lessons.title: Clickable prototypes
lessons.concept: Link screens with interactions so people can click through like a real app.

lessons.title: Transitions and feedback
lessons.concept: Small animations show what changed and where things came from.

lessons.title: Testing and handoff
lessons.concept: Test the prototype with users, then hand off clear specs to developers.

lessons.title: Variables and lists
lessons.concept: Python keeps values in variables and many values in lists.

lessons.title: Functions and loops
lessons.concept: def makes a function, and for loops repeat work for each item.

lessons.title: Libraries for AI
lessons.concept: Libraries like NumPy, pandas and scikit-learn do the heavy work for data and models.

lessons.title: Examples and labels
lessons.concept: A model learns from examples; labels are the right answers attached to them.

lessons.title: Cleaning data
lessons.concept: Remove duplicates, fix mistakes and handle missing values before training.

lessons.title: Training and test sets
lessons.concept: Keep some data aside to test the model on examples it never saw.

lessons.title: What is machine learning?
lessons.concept: Instead of writing rules, we show examples and the computer finds the pattern.

lessons.title: Training a model
lessons.concept: Training adjusts the model step by step to make fewer mistakes on the examples.

lessons.title: Neural networks
lessons.concept: Neural networks stack layers of simple units to learn complex patterns like images and speech.

lessons.title: Bias
lessons.concept: If training data is unfair, the model can be unfair too.

lessons.title: Privacy
lessons.concept: Collect only the data you need, and protect it, especially for children.

lessons.title: Safety and honesty
lessons.concept: AI can be wrong; show uncertainty, let humans check, and never hide that it is AI.

lessons.title: Cells and formulas
lessons.concept: Each cell holds a value; formulas like =SUM(A1:A5) calculate from other cells.

lessons.title: Sorting, filters and IF
lessons.concept: Sort and filter to find answers, and IF to label rows by a rule.

lessons.title: Pivot tables
lessons.concept: Pivot tables summarise many rows, like average score per class, in a few clicks.

lessons.title: Data in Python
lessons.concept: Python lists and dictionaries hold data you can count, sum and sort.
lessons.try_it_starter_code:
const temps = [21, 25, 19, 23];
console.log(Math.max(...temps));

lessons.title: pandas DataFrames
lessons.concept: A DataFrame is a table; pandas reads CSV files and filters rows easily.
lessons.try_it_starter_code:
const students = [{ n: 'Aya', g: 9 }, { n: 'Omar', g: 10 }, { n: 'Mona', g: 9 }];
console.log(students.filter(s => s.g === 9).length);

lessons.title: Grouping and merging
lessons.concept: groupby summarises by category, and merge joins two tables on a shared column.

lessons.title: SELECT and WHERE
lessons.concept: SELECT picks columns, WHERE picks rows.

lessons.title: Aggregates and GROUP BY
lessons.concept: COUNT, SUM and AVG summarise; GROUP BY makes one row per group.

lessons.title: Joins for analysis
lessons.concept: Joins combine tables, like students with their scores, to answer bigger questions.

lessons.title: Choosing a chart
lessons.concept: Bar charts compare, line charts show change over time, and pie charts show parts of a whole.

lessons.title: Clear and honest charts
lessons.concept: Start bar axes at zero, use few colours, and highlight the key point.

lessons.title: Dashboards and stories
lessons.concept: A dashboard shows the few numbers that matter, in an order that tells a story.

lessons.title: What is a bug?
lessons.concept: A bug is when software does not do what it should; testers find them before users do.

lessons.title: Types of testing
lessons.concept: Functional tests check features; others check speed, security and usability.

lessons.title: Testing by risk
lessons.concept: Test the most important and most risky parts first and most often.

lessons.title: Writing test cases
lessons.concept: A test case lists steps, input data and the expected result.

lessons.title: Boundaries and partitions
lessons.concept: Test just inside and outside the limits, and one value from each group.
lessons.try_it_starter_code:
const valid = age => age >= 13 && age <= 18;
console.log([12, 13, 18, 19].map(valid).join(','));

lessons.title: Great bug reports
lessons.concept: A good report has steps, expected vs actual, environment, severity and evidence.

lessons.title: Assertions
lessons.concept: An assertion checks that a value is what you expect and fails loudly if not.

lessons.title: UI automation
lessons.concept: Tools like Playwright click buttons and type text in a real browser to test pages.
lessons.try_it_starter_code:
const steps = ['open login', 'type email', 'type password', 'click sign in'];
console.log(steps.length);

lessons.title: Tests in CI
lessons.concept: Continuous integration runs every test on each change and blocks merges that break them.

lessons.title: Requests and responses
lessons.concept: Send a request to an API and check the status code and the data that comes back.

lessons.title: Testing errors
lessons.concept: Send bad input on purpose and check the API answers with clear, safe errors.
lessons.try_it_starter_code:
const response = { status: 400, body: { code: 'VALIDATION_FAILED' } };
console.log(response.status === 400 && response.body.code ? 'ok' : 'bug');

lessons.title: Contracts and load
lessons.concept: Contract tests make sure the API keeps its promised shape, and load tests check it under many users.

lessons.title: Goals and rules
lessons.concept: Every game has a goal, rules and a challenge that makes reaching the goal fun.

lessons.title: Difficulty and flow
lessons.concept: Good games get harder slowly, keeping players between bored and frustrated.

lessons.title: Playtesting
lessons.concept: Watch people play your game and change what confuses or bores them.

lessons.title: Score and lives
lessons.concept: Variables track the score and lives, and change when things happen.

lessons.title: Movement and the game loop
lessons.concept: Each frame the game reads input, moves things and draws them again.

lessons.title: Collisions
lessons.concept: Two boxes collide when they overlap on both the x and y axes.

lessons.title: Scenes and GameObjects
lessons.concept: A Unity scene holds GameObjects; components like Transform and Sprite give them position and look.

lessons.title: Scripts and input
lessons.concept: MonoBehaviour scripts use Start once and Update every frame to read input and move.

lessons.title: Physics and UI
lessons.concept: Rigidbodies and colliders handle physics, and the UI system shows score and menus.

lessons.title: Polish
lessons.concept: Sound, small effects and smooth menus make a game feel finished.

lessons.title: Platforms and builds
lessons.concept: Build your game for web, PC or mobile, and test each build.

lessons.title: Feedback and updates
lessons.concept: Listen to players, fix bugs and update the game over time.

mentors.title: Senior Frontend Engineer
mentors.bio: Sara builds web apps used by millions of people. She loves helping beginners turn their first idea into a real page and believes every good developer starts by being curious.

mentors.title: Frontend Developer
mentors.bio: Omar started coding at school by making small games in the browser. Today he builds websites for startups and enjoys explaining code with simple, everyday examples.

mentors.title: Backend Engineer
mentors.bio: Nadia designs the systems that keep apps running behind the scenes. She enjoys logic puzzles and teaching students how data moves through an app.

mentors.title: Product Designer
mentors.bio: Layla designs apps that are simple and friendly. She teaches students to watch how people use things and to sketch many ideas before choosing one.

mentors.title: Machine Learning Engineer
mentors.bio: Karim teaches computers to recognise images and speech. He likes showing students that the maths they learn at school is what makes AI work.

mentors.title: Data Analyst
mentors.bio: Hana finds stories hidden in numbers. She helps students ask good questions and answer them with clear charts.

mentors.title: Mobile Developer
mentors.bio: Tarek has built apps for shops, schools and clinics. He loves seeing students install their first app on their own phone.

mentors.title: QA Engineer
mentors.bio: Mariam finds the bugs before users do. She teaches students to think like detectives: try the edge cases, write clear steps, and never trust that it just works.

mentors.title: Game Developer
mentors.bio: Youssef has shipped mobile games played by thousands of people. He helps students turn a fun idea into a small playable game, one level at a time.

items.skills: Attention to detail, Writing test cases, Bug reports
items.description: Careful Code Lab tests apps before they are released. In this practice role you would find bugs and write clear reports.
Cairo Cloud Works builds the servers behind delivery apps. In this practice role you would add simple API endpoints and save data in a database.

items.skills: Flutter or React Native, Screen layouts, Testing on phones
items.description: Pocket Apps Co. makes mobile apps for sports clubs. In this practice role you would build simple screens and test them on different phones.

items.skills: Python, Data preparation, Training simple models
items.description: Smart Nile Labs builds models that sort photos of plants. In this practice role you would prepare data and check how well a model works.

items.skills: Unity or Godot, Game logic, Playtesting
items.description: Pyramid Play Games makes small puzzle games. In this practice role you would code simple game rules and fix bugs that players report.
